lines.en: Nirvana looked utterly shocked. Their mental attack had rebounded off the [Fourth Wall], and the White Pure Star Energy that followed had left wounds both large and small.
“······What the hell did you do?”
“I didn't do anything in particular. It's the power of a story.”
“What?”
I didn't particularly believe in the Salvation Church's doctrine, but there was one thing I agreed with.
“You said it yourself. ‘Strength and weakness are determined by stories.’”
Just as even a warrior with high Constitution is easy prey for a mage if the warrior lacks a magic defense skill, strength and weakness ultimately depend on the histories those people have lived.
“It's your fault for not leveling up your melee skills in this life. This is what happens when you only target Yoo Joonghyuk's weaknesses.”
Even I hadn't expected things to work out this way.

Something had influenced Nirvana's development, turning them into a counter to Yoo Joonghyuk. But precisely because Nirvana had become Yoo Joonghyuk's counter, they now stood no chance of defeating me.
Nirvana's gaze wavered as they picked up on something in my tone.
They glared silently at me, then spoke.
“I know your name. Kim Dokja.”
“Starting with introductions? Fine, Nirvana Moebius. Looks like you're willing to talk now?”
The light went out in the mandala suspended in the air.
A reincarnator wasn't a reincarnator for nothing.
As if a switch had flipped to another self, the agitated Nirvana vanished. Before me stood a Nirvana who had already regained their composure.
“Several nebulae warned me about you. Told me to be careful. Of course, I didn't think you'd actually appear.”
Several ‘nebulae,’ huh······.
Apparently, I really had drawn some attention.
“How did you obtain such a powerful mental barrier? Until now, Anna Croft was the only one who had resisted infection by my thoughts.”

I smiled wryly at the familiar name. That woman had already gotten involved with a reincarnator. It wasn't strange. Anna Croft would surely have already begun her scheduled contacts with the world's powerful figures through a communication medium.
That woman would sell her soul to the devil if it meant saving the world.
Perhaps reading something in my expression, Nirvana spoke.
“You······know the Prophet. Just what are you? Don't tell me you're a regressor? Or······.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ takes an interest in the conversation.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ quietly observes the situation.]
The information filtering would have begun lifting little by little around now.
Information about regressors and reincarnators would start reaching the constellations, too. Though the perceptive higher-ups in the great nebulae would already know.
Looking at me, Nirvana continued.
“What an intriguing sentient being. To arouse the curiosity of someone who has lived for hundreds of years······.”
“You talk too much. That's why you'll keep having trouble getting Yoo Joonghyuk.”
“Kahahaha! I shall accept you into the Salvation Church.”
[A constellation reciting Buddhist scriptures amid ascetic suffering expresses curiosity about you.]
Earlier, I would have gladly accepted that offer. But.
“I'll pass. One of the beings supporting me absolutely loathes your sponsor.”
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ shows hostility toward the constellation sponsor of ‘Nirvana Moebius.’]
Nirvana's mouth fell slightly open.
“The Monkey King? Why is he following you around?”
“I don't know either.”
“······You intrigue me even more now. Serve under me. Together with Yoo Joonghyuk.”
“I said no.”
“Are you not curious about this world's secrets? I can help you survive even after this world ends. Regardless of whether you fail the scenarios.”
It was a tempting offer.
If I hadn't been a ‘reader,’ I might have accepted long ago.
“I shall allow you, too, to become ‘one’ with me!”
Behind Nirvana's back, the mandala began shining brightly again.
Hundreds of faces protruded from the enormous, slowly rotating mandala. The anguished faces of vengeful spirits screamed. They were all humans who had become ‘one’ with Nirvana.
“Shut up and come at me, you perverted bastard.”
“If you will not agree, I shall have to take you by force.”
Despite their disadvantage, Nirvana's expression remained entirely composed.
My opponent was a ‘reincarnator,’ after all. Having lived countless lives, they possessed a far better instinct for combat than I did.
As time passed, they would begin reading my movements, and the fight would turn against me.
Then the answer was to end the fight before that happened.
Whoooosh!
The mandala, wrapped in white energy, drove toward my chest.
Without hesitation, I hurled myself toward the mandala's strike.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Miniaturization Lv.1’!]
[Your body shrinks under the effects of Miniaturization.]
My body rapidly shrank, and the strike missed.
Nirvana laughed.
“······You even have a little trick like that?”
Was it really just a little trick?
[All your equipment transforms to fit your size under the effects of Miniaturization.]
[The duration is shortened due to the low skill level.]
[Miniaturization can last for 2 minutes.]
The reason I had passed over all those good skills to choose [Miniaturization].
It was because only [Miniaturization] could turn me into the most powerful being I knew.
“I'll select Bookmark number 5, ‘Kyrgios Rodgraim.’”
[Your physical composition has been confirmed to resemble that of the corresponding character.]
[The character’s level is too high to fully reproduce the skill’s level.]
[The level of the activated skill is forcibly adjusted.]
Surging White Pure energy settled in my heart. The power to shatter the heavens and bring down thunder. I could see Nirvana's face growing pale before the tremendous lightning energy.
“Still look like a little trick to you?”
No matter how strong Nirvana was, surpassing Kyrgios's power at this point was impossible.
[The exclusive skill ‘Electrification (電人化) Lv.10’ has been activated.]
Bzzzzzt!
As fierce lightning crackled over my entire body, thunderclouds began gathering around my fist.
If I couldn't make use of the reincarnator, I was better off eliminating them here.
I drove my fist toward Nirvana with all my strength.
“Pray you're born human again.”
Bzzzzzt―KABOOOOM!
The thundercloud, vaporizing everything around it as it advanced, exploded against Nirvana's side.

Nirvana let out a terrible scream, and I heard the incarnations shouting. Miniaturization's low level meant I couldn't produce as much power as I had against Orochi, but given the skill involved, the attack was still devastating.
When the dust cloud cleared amid the explosions, Nirvana lay sprawled some distance away with a massive hole in their side.
····Still alive? After taking that?
“Guaaaaagh!”
Blood clots gushed from their mouth. They seemed badly hurt, but I wasn't satisfied. It was strange. Even a reincarnator shouldn't have survived that attack.
I saw lotus petals growing little by little over their body. In an instant, I thought I understood what had happened. Shouldn't probability prevent them from using that stigma?
This bastard, don't tell me?
“My memories, in a place like this······.”
A grating voice, teeth grinding.
Seeing the faint sparks crackling over the lotus petals, I thought I understood how they had survived.
[Story Payment].
In that brief instant, they had borrowed power from their sponsor, paying with the Stories they had accumulated.
“······We shall meet again.”
Their body was being enveloped in enormous lotus petals. I hurled myself toward them.
Bzzzzt―CRUNCH!
My fist pierced their heart, but Nirvana was smiling.
With a face contorted like one of Buddhism's Four World-Protecting Kings (護世四王).
“You will pay for defying the ‘present.’ In the most terrible way.”
Beginning at the heart I had burst, their body dissolved into nothingness (無化), then began turning into lotus petals.
I reached out with a hand shrouded in Electrification and seized their disappearing left arm.
“Wait!”
Rrrriiiip!
The next instant, Nirvana vanished, leaving only a torn-off left arm and drifting lotus petals behind.
[The character ‘Nirvana Moebius’ has used the stigma ‘No Ownership Lv.7.’]
No Ownership.
A stigma that discarded some of one's memories to escape danger.
They had escaped me by paying with memories of their reincarnations.
“L-Leader-nim!”
“Leader-nim! Where have you gone!”
The bewildered Salvation Church followers were falling apart. Some were already fleeing. Seeing the being they believed in defeated before their eyes must have dealt them an enormous mental shock.
Watching the Salvation Church followers retreat, I finally managed a sigh of relief.
Smoke rose from my body as [Miniaturization] and [Bookmark] deactivated simultaneously.
My overworked muscles felt torn to shreds, protesting in pain.
I hadn't killed Nirvana, but I had gained a few things.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ cannot hide his joy at your victory.]
[You have received a donation of 10000 coins.]
The new incarnations who had witnessed my victory were looking at one another in disbelief.
“The Salvation Church's leader lost!”
“Who the hell is that incarnation?”
“Wait, that face, that's······!”
Someone pointed at me and shouted.
“The ugliest king!”
I ignored them and looked for Yoo Joonghyuk.
In the distance, I saw Yoo Joonghyuk staggering, freed from his paralysis.
That damned sunfish. He was never any help when it mattered.
“Hey, you all right?”
Pressing a hand to his forehead as if his head hurt, Yoo Joonghyuk asked.
“The reincarnator?”
“Escaped.”
“······Pathetic. You let them get away?”
“Try helping before you say shit like that.”
Yoo Joonghyuk's expression was grave.
“We need to pursue them immediately. Their goal isn't to clear the scenarios.”
“I know that, you bastard.”
“You knew and still let them go? If we don't catch the reincarnator before the tenth scenario ends, Seoul will······.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ belatedly comes to her senses.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ wants to explain why she came here.]
At Uriel's words, Yoo Joonghyuk and I looked up into the air at the same time.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ needs your help!]
The limitations of indirect messages made it impossible to understand the precise circumstances, but guessing what had happened wasn't difficult.
Uriel was Jung Heewon's sponsor. Yet Uriel, who should have been with Jung Heewon, had come here, and we had lost contact with Jung Heewon.
That meant······.
“Min Jiwon-ssi. Do you happen to know where Jung Heewon-ssi is?”
But Min Jiwon still hadn't come to her senses.
No luck here.
“Yoo Joonghyuk, protect me.”
“What?”
I immediately closed my eyes and focused my consciousness.
After repeatedly practicing falling asleep, I was getting quite used to it.
Darkness closed in from every direction as I felt my body slowly sinking toward the ground.
The moment I felt myself slipping into a light sleep, I used [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint].
I had to find a voice.
A voice calling for me.
But I heard no voices.
I was growing more anxious.
I'd told them to think of me first if we got separated······ Had something really gone wrong?
‘Dokja-ssi.’
At last, someone called me.
My vision distorted as [Third-Person Observer Viewpoint] activated. I groaned in horror at the image that appeared the next moment.
「Fwooooosh!」
Pure white flames surging across the entire screen.
The stigma of judgement, which melted everything, was burning the world.
There was no need to ask.
This was unmistakably Jung Heewon's [Hell Flames Ignition].
Thank goodness. Jung Heewon was still alive.
But······something was strange.
I wasn't seeing through Jung Heewon's eyes?
A moment later, Jung Heewon emerged from the flames, and I saw a lotus pattern glowing on her forehead.
······Damn it, Nirvana had already gotten to her.
Well, even Yoo Joonghyuk had fallen victim. It would have been strange if Jung Heewon had escaped unscathed. But a question remained.
Then who on earth had called me?
「“Jung Heewon-ssi?”」
An earnest soldier's voice. It was Lee Hyunsung.
「Rrrrrrumble!」
An explosion rang out, and the screen shook as if it would burst. The nearby incarnations exploded into chunks of flesh, and everything the hellish flames touched went up in flames.
Judging by the location, they were somewhere I couldn't reach immediately to help.
It was obvious what would happen at this rate.
Jung Heewon, driven out of her mind by [Thought Infection], wouldn't hesitate, and the innocent Lee Hyunsung stood helpless before her blade.
Damn it, what should I do?
“Guh!”
Suddenly, the darkness lifted, and the entire screen shattered.
I opened my eyes, fighting a strong urge to vomit, and saw Yoo Joonghyuk scowling fiercely.
“What am I supposed to do when you suddenly fall asleep like that?”
Saliva dribbled from my mouth, and my solar plexus hurt terribly.
Had this bastard just hit me to wake me up?
······Wait, hit?
A realization flashed through my mind.
Right. That was it.
I really hated it, but there was only one way to save them both.
I urged Yoo Joonghyuk.
“Hey, hit me again. Really hard.”
Had that left room for misunderstanding?
Then I should make myself clear.
“No, kill me right now.”
Everyone has a few words that have influenced them.
Lee Hyunsung had such words, too.
For example, when he first became a university student, these were the things Lee Hyunsung heard most often in his undergraduate classes.
‘Everyone, you must become creative people!’
‘Think thoughts that no one else thinks!’
‘You must be able to leap up from where you are right now!’
At the time, Lee Hyunsung thought.
‘So······how am I supposed to do that?’
For Lee Hyunsung, who had gone to school, eaten, and slept at fixed times since childhood, society's demands came far too abruptly.
Until now, they'd told him to follow the prescribed course. Why were they suddenly forcing him to do something he'd never done before?
What even was creativity.
What did it mean to think thoughts that others didn't?
Why had the world suddenly become a place where he had to do those things to survive?
Then what had I been doing all this time?
Lee Hyunsung drifted throughout university, and naturally ended up in the military.
‘From what I can see, you're born for military life. Try applying to the officer commissioning program.’
What would his life be like now if the administrative officer hadn't said that to him then?
There was no way to know.
He could know nothing about a future he hadn't chosen.
In any case, he became a soldier as if it were inevitable, and had lived without regretting that choice.
For someone who found society and people difficult, the military was comparatively comfortable.
When Lee Hyunsung returned after passing the officer commissioning program, the administrative officer congratulated him with these words.
‘Second Lieutenant Lee-nim. Whenever you're unsure, always follow the manual. Then, at least, people won't hold you responsible, Second Lieutenant Lee-nim.’

Had those words taken the place of a toast? His memories were as hazy as what he'd eaten for lunch a week ago. Still, if he could meet the administrative officer again now, there was one thing he wanted to ask.
‘Administrative Officer, what am I supposed to do in a situation like this?’
Watching the approaching flames of Hell Flames Ignition, Lee Hyunsung bit his lip.
‘I don't have a manual for this situation.’
Thinking that reciting the soldier's creed had been easier, Lee Hyunsung shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Jung Heewon-ssi! Come to your senses! Please!”
But just as the soldier's creed failed to move soldiers' hearts, his voice failed to reach Jung Heewon.
Fwoooosh!
He ducked behind a building just in time. Hellish flames blanketed the ground, and the nearby incarnations burned in agony.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“Save me!”
But Lee Hyunsung couldn't save any of them.
Watching the deaths unfolding before his eyes, Lee Hyunsung realized once again that all the ‘justice’ lying dormant within him was merely a ‘manual.’
Jung Heewon's figure approached, rippling like a mirage in the heat.
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ watches you silently.]
Under that silent gaze, Lee Hyunsung bit his lip.
‘Dokja-ssi. What on earth should I do at a time like this?’
Should he fight?
Could he stop her?

As Lee Hyunsung watched Jung Heewon approach, his tightly clenched fists trembled. What that trembling meant, where this persistent hesitation came from, why he couldn't leave this place—Lee Hyunsung understood none of it.
Perhaps the world wasn't what was difficult.
What was difficult was Lee Hyunsung himself.
‘Dokja-ssi, please tell me the answer!’

Though he knew it couldn't happen, Lee Hyunsung prayed like a reservist hoping the weather would miraculously worsen enough to cancel training. Then, astonishingly, he heard the voice he had been desperately waiting for.
―Lee Hyunsung-ssi.
He thought he was hearing things.
―Can you hear me?
But it wasn't a hallucination.
He looked around, but there was nowhere the voice could be coming from.
In other words, the voice was coming from inside his head.
“Dokja-ssi!”
Could this be another enemy trap?
But even if it was an enemy trick, he wanted to believe it.
―Let's think while you run away for now. There are two ways.
Lee Hyunsung instinctively sprang to his feet and ran.
It wasn't a trap.
Only that man began a conversation this way.
Jung Heewon was pursuing him, but he was no longer afraid.
His breathing quickly steadied, and his mind was ready to receive new orders. His tense muscles began swelling, breathing hard.
―One way is to kill Jung Heewon-ssi.
“······A familiar option.”
Kim Dokja was always like this.
He had been that way since they first met.
He always offered the safest, cruelest solution first.
Then he made his companions reject it themselves.
“And the second is to keep running away, I assume?”
―······That's right.
“Then I'll take the third way, as always.”
With Kim Dokja's solutions, the third was always the right answer.
Someone who thought of a third way in any situation. That was Kim Dokja.
So Lee Hyunsung believed in him this time, too.
But.
―Lee Hyunsung-ssi. This time, there is no third way.
Of course there was a third way.
I just had to wait for the right moment.
[‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint Stage 3’ is active.]
[‘First-Person Supporting Character Viewpoint’ is currently incomplete.]
Of all opponents, it had to be Jung Heewon using [Hell Flames Ignition].
It couldn't have been a worse matchup.
Though, really, anyone else would have had the same problem.
“······Why are you always like this!”
Lee Hyunsung was shouting between ragged breaths.
Fwooosh!
Through the first-person viewpoint, I felt the full heat of Hell Flames Ignition.
Jung Heewon swung her sword as if she meant to turn all of Seoul into a sea of fire. Strictly speaking, the first and second options I had offered would bring essentially the same result.
Whether Lee Hyunsung killed Jung Heewon or ran away.
Left like this, Jung Heewon would die when her magic power ran out of control.
In the end, one of the two would die.
That was the scenario of that damned ‘Nirvana.’
“Kill Jung Heewon-ssi? Did you come to me just to give that sort of advice?”
Jung Heewon was approaching.
I'd been a little unsure when she was an ally, but now that she was an enemy, I could tell for certain.
Jung Heewon, the Judge of Evil, was strong.
Even without using [Hour of Judgement], she possessed [Demon Slaying].
On top of that, the ability to mercilessly unleash Uriel's stigma, [Hell Flames Ignition].
She was, in both name and deed, the most powerful fighter in my party.
Subduing Jung Heewon in this berserk state without killing her would be nearly impossible even for Yoo Joonghyuk as he was now.
“I cannot accept that solution.”
Where had he found that courage?
Lee Hyunsung began approaching Jung Heewon.
―Wait, Lee Hyunsung-ssi!
“Jung Heewon-ssi! Come to your senses!”
Lee Hyunsung ran toward Jung Heewon. As if he were angry with me, as if he were angry with himself for trusting the ‘manual’ that was me, he ran.
KABOOOOM!
Lee Hyunsung's [Great Mountain Push] collided with Jung Heewon's [Hell Flames Ignition].
But even his palm, capable of pushing a great mountain, couldn't break through an archangel's flames. Soon, his right arm began dripping away, shedding pure white light as it melted.
“Jung Heewon-ssi!”
Lee Hyunsung's cry was agonized and desperate. Disregarding his lost right arm, he reached out again with his left. I shouted urgently.
―Lee Hyunsung-ssi, if you run away, one of you can survive.
“I refuse.”
―No one will hold you responsible for running away.
“I refuse!”
―Haven't you been treating me like a manual? Then listen to me!
“That isn't the kind of manual I wanted!”
Lee Hyunsung's answer was unexpected.
At the same time, it was an answer that couldn't have been more like him.
Everyone contains contradictions.
Those who faithfully follow manuals actually hate them more than anyone. Just as creative people actually want to submit to the system more than anyone.
And when they break through that contradiction, a 「Story」 begins.
Rooooar!
“I can't give up like that! Even if things turn out badly. Even if I die here!”
However sturdy Lee Hyunsung was, he couldn't withstand [Hell Flames Ignition], which had melted even Shin Yoosung. His left arm soon melted away, and even his right leg began to melt.
Still, Lee Hyunsung resisted.
Like a moth throwing itself into a flame, he tried desperately to reach Jung Heewon.
As everything below his right knee vanished and he staggered, I spoke to him.
―I see. Well done.
Lee Hyunsung didn't answer.
I smiled bitterly and spoke.
―Because that is the ‘third way.’
The third way wasn't something he could use just because I told him about it.
Lee Hyunsung had to make that decision himself.
In truth, even I wasn't sure whether it would work.
Nevertheless, I had chosen this path because, the moment he saw Jung Heewon, I had discovered a faint, aching emotion stirring in Lee Hyunsung's heart.
―It's a way you found yourself, without a manual.
Collapsing amid the flames, Lee Hyunsung smiled.
“Dokja-ssi, thank you for everything.”
At that moment, I could feel, together with Lee Hyunsung, the elation rising within his body.
An emotion only a person who had broken through their own contradictions and answered in defiance of death could reach.

Perhaps this feeling was the authentic existence (實存) Nirvana so desperately wanted to attain. Nirvana would have been dumbfounded to see it. They had infected Jung Heewon, yet it was Lee Hyunsung who was living in the present more fully than anyone.
―No need to thank me. This is only the beginning.
With this, the requirements for the Story's beginning were met.
But it was up to the audience to decide whether this story would continue.
The one being who had been reading Lee Hyunsung with a more sensitive gaze than anyone else.
―Master of Steel. Most steadfast being in the sublime <Star Stream>.
I slowly continued.
―Isn't it time you answered?
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ listens to your words.]
The constellation ‘Master of Steel.’
Ruler of Orichalcum, the hardest planet in the universe, and sponsor of Lee Hyunsung, the Steel Sword Emperor.
I went straight to the point.
―Give your incarnation a chance.
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ hums in thought.]
―I know what you fear. You're afraid of rashly shouldering the probability.
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ closes their eyes.]
―But how long will you keep worrying about what the surrounding nebulae think? Will you sit idly by like this until the scenarios come to their end?
Lee Hyunsung had done his part.
Now the choice lay with his sponsor.
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ acknowledges the courage of the incarnation ‘Lee Hyunsung.’]
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ nevertheless says that the time has not yet come.]
I had expected that.
In fact, Lee Hyunsung was still too weak for his awakening.
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ believes that the incarnation ‘Lee Hyunsung’ will be unable to bear the constellation's Story.]
The Story of steel was hard and heavy.
As the constellation said, Lee Hyunsung wouldn't be able to withstand it.
If he were alone, that is.
―I'll bear it with him.
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ looks at you.]
The Master of Steel remained silent, seemingly thinking something over.
Then, a moment later, a message came.
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ nods.]
And tingling sparks began crackling around us.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ prepares for attribute evolution.]
[A ‘Story’ is required to evolve into the corresponding attribute.]
[The constellation ‘Master of Steel’ bestows a Story trial.]
[The Story ‘Proof of Steel’ begins!]
A silver torrent was rising from Lee Hyunsung's body. Watching that dazzling brilliance, I recalled a scene I had once read in ‘Ways of Survival.’
Who had it been?
One of the characters had once asked Yoo Joonghyuk this question.
「“Why is Lee Hyunsung-ajusshi called the Steel Sword Emperor? He doesn't use a sword, does he?”」
Even in the original ‘Ways of Survival,’ Lee Hyunsung had never used a sword.
Nevertheless, Lee Hyunsung's nickname was the Steel Sword Emperor.
「“Lee Hyunsung doesn't need a sword.”」
Crrrrunch!
Pure white steel began growing from Lee Hyunsung's melted arms and leg.
Then, like a covering of scales, the growing steel spread over his entire body.
Lee Hyunsung's body was becoming like a single enormous sword (巨劍).
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ activates the stigma ‘Steel Transformation (鋼鐵化)’!]
The one sword that would never break, whatever trial it struck.
If Yoo Joonghyuk had been here, he would surely have said this.
「“Because he himself is the sword.”」
Crrrunch!
A newly grown skin of steel. As if he were being reborn as another species, Lee Hyunsung's body was being made anew.
Steel Transformation (鋼鐵化).

Only the first stage, ‘Armor (甲冑),’ had activated, but even that was no ordinary power. Once Lee Hyunsung fully mastered the first stage, he would be tougher than Gong Pildu's Armed Fortress and could survive a blow from Yoo Joonghyuk's Splitting the Sky Sword.
The problem was that the first stage hadn't fully activated yet.
―That is the true ‘stigma’ you need to master, Lee Hyunsung-ssi.
Quickly grasping the situation, Lee Hyunsung took a stance and stepped back.
[‘Steel Transformation’ is not yet complete.]
[This stigma can only be used by beings who have achieved a Story.]
Every sponsor provided stigmas to their incarnation.
Some stigmas were bestowed as gifts, while others could only be used after fulfilling demanding conditions.
The Master of Steel's ‘Steel Transformation’ was one of those demanding stigmas.
[‘First Proof of Steel’ begins.]
Because this stigma required an indirect experience of the ‘proof’ the constellation had undergone.
<Proof of Steel>
1.「True steel shall be born through tens of thousands of quenchings」
Unlike a scenario, it was a sentence tossed at us without explanation.
Lee Hyunsung asked, seemingly confused.
“What does this mean?”
―Quenching basically means heating something to a high temperature, then cooling it.
“Don't tell me······.”
―What you're thinking is probably right. Stay focused.
In a sense, perhaps it was fortunate that Jung Heewon had become Lee Hyunsung's opponent.
Lee Hyunsung's face went pale.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ takes an interest in a Story from another world.]
[The constellation ‘Defense Master’ wonders whether it really is tougher than them.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ clasps her hands anxiously.]
Along with the constellations' messages, blazing hellfire rolled in like a wave.
Rrrrrroar!
Perhaps the value for Jung Heewon's [Hell Flames Ignition] had risen in the meantime; the tidal wave of fire had grown deeper and more savage.
Asphalt melted into the pure white flames, adding impurities. The clumps, mixed together in the intense heat, were swept up in the waves and became menacing weapons.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!

The silver armor was scorched in an instant and began melting. Foreign matter spattering here and there pierced the armor like bullets and melted Lee Hyunsung's insides. Whenever the armor melted, new steel grew to fill the gaps, but that didn't mean he suffered no damage.
Blood flowed from Lee Hyunsung's mouth.

If his Steel Transformation had been complete, even [Hell Flames Ignition] wouldn't have fazed him. But it wasn't yet. [Hell Flames Ignition] was one of the highest-ranking fire stigmas, after all. Simply not collapsing was astonishing.
Lee Hyunsung screamed as he retreated one step at a time.
Watching him was painful for me, too, but it wasn't time yet.
Lee Hyunsung's steel was glowing red.
A little more, just a little more······.
[The temperature has exceeded the threshold!]
There.
[Quenching begins.]
The foundation of steel was quenching.
The essence of this Story was enduring heat above the threshold until he achieved a complete body of steel.
―Hold on! You can do it!
The only consolation was that, fortunately, Lee Hyunsung wasn't an ‘evil person.’
[Hell Flames Ignition], a stigma with the attributes of ‘fire’ and ‘holiness.’
Had he been branded with the mark of evil and fully exposed to the heat of [Hell Flames Ignition], Lee Hyunsung would already have been reduced to a handful of liquefied ash.
While Lee Hyunsung screamed, I quickly examined Jung Heewon's information.
[The character ‘Jung Heewon’ is currently affected by ‘Thought Infection.’]
[The character ‘Jung Heewon’ has lost her reason.]
[The trauma of the character ‘Jung Heewon’ has been fully exposed.]
······That son of a bitch had torn a person's mind to shreds.
「I can't forgive them······.」
To anchor a person's time in the ‘present,’ Nirvana's [Thought Infection] dragged every dark corner of their mind to the surface.
「I have to kill them.」
